visualReview.notes: Inspected seven current portable views. The Stoney Street E-plan, central stair and gable, arched openings and linked brick ranges read clearly. The aerial view shows the enclosed court and the open recesses between ranges.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Inspected seven current shared-material views, including the bounded dated geographic placement. Pale ashlar, red brick, iron rails and slate roof planes remain distinct. The ground overlay shows the full irregular envelope and mapped inner court.

mediumFiReview.notes: Inspected 23 current context, detail and transition frames. All four detail levels retain the whole ensemble, courtyard opening, main stair, gable and roof silhouettes. At nearer levels, ashlar surrounds, rounded heads, casement bars and thin rails become visible.

geographicReview.notes: OpenStreetMap relation 3581525 supplies 62 outer and 18 inner court corners. The Stoney Street axis and building ring establish the site. The unmasked original field view shows the stair and front retaining base meeting the ground. The stone basement is seated as grade rises toward the rear.

fidelityReview.scope: The Adams Building in the Lace Market as documented by the 2008 exterior photographs. Includes the three projecting Stoney Street bays and their open forecourt, the attached rear warehouse ranges, and the independently mapped courtyard. Historic railings and front stairs are modeled where visible. Interiors and adjacent buildings are outside scope.
fidelityReview.notes: The early 2008 color photographs document the stone-trimmed red brick front and the rounded, tall rear elevations. Historic England supplies the E-plan entrance, stone rail details and slate roof type. Exact heights, hidden elevations, roof subdivisions and local stair grades are estimates.

imageryReview.notes: Two existing Qualla public-domain originals by Superhasn and Smashman match pinned Commons records and exact native SHA-1. Both show the building in 2008. Sculpture close-ups and unrelated images were excluded.

validation.sharedCaptureScope: 2008 Adams Building street elevations, irregular mapped envelope and open interior court

limitations: Two verified public-domain Qualla photographs from April and June 2008 guide the modeled front and rear exterior. Historic England’s written record supplies the E-plan front and the character of the slate roofs, stone dressings and arched windows.

The mapped outline and inner court are retained. The other recesses remain open where the outline turns around them. Heights, roof subdivisions, exact stair and railing positions, and unphotographed walls are proportional estimates.
The independent terrain field is unchanged. Its reference near Stoney Street provides the approximate elevation basis for the entrance steps. Coarse grades are not a survey.
The asset is a dated exterior. Recesses, dressings and ironwork use original geometry and shared materials. No photographic pixels or museum interior details are included.
